reference_use.conclusion:
The snapshot (project d8d46c95, Mathlib 25730c7c) contains the frozen Ch06 Contract, byte-identical to the workspace Contract and Submission. Only GMT.Ch06.main_theorem and its 12 children are reserved in the DAG, so the bare lpf_* names are free.

The child scope (import GMT.Ch06.Submission plus the replayed namespace and opens) gives the contract notions and SimonGMT Ch01 Densities, Ch03 Rectifiable (HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt, blowUpMap, CountablyRectifiable, .unique) and Ch06 (NVector, simpleNVector, nVectorPushforward, nVectorPushforward_simple, TestFormOn, GeometricCurrentOn, support). Chapter02.IsSimonSubmanifold is not in scope, so C¹ pieces are stated as C¹ maps that are antilipschitz on open sets.

Instance checks:
- NVector carries the operator norm over the ContinuousAlternatingMap norm, so ‖simpleNVector v‖² is the Gram determinant and ‖L_#ξ‖ is the area Jacobian.
- volume on Eucl n is measureSpaceOfInnerProductSpace, and μHE[n] = volume there.
- μHE[0] = μH[0].

Mathlib provides the fundamental lemma (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero), measurable_fderiv, hausdorffMeasure_of_dimH_lt, Hadamard via Orientation.abs_volumeForm_apply_le, normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent and LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi.

SimonGMT provides Rademacher, Lipschitz image bounds and image measurability (Ch02/Lipschitz). It provides the full Euclidean area formula with fibre sums and its a.e.-measurability (Ch02/AreaDomain: weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn, ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension) and null critical images (Ch02/AreaLipschitz: area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero). It also provides the upper density theorem (Ch01 simon_theorem_3_6), Lusin (Ch01/Lusin), and the C¹-cover-to-rectifiable direction (Ch03/SubmanifoldCover).

SimonGMT does not provide:
- Lemma 1.2 ⇒, Theorem 1.6/1.9 existence, or the rectifiable area formula; these are the new children.
- A packaged C¹ approximation theorem: Whitney machinery exists in Ch02/WhitneyExtension.lean, but that file is not built.

All 11 child statements pass the lexical validator and elaborate in the comparator child scope. The parent assembly from 3 children is kernel-checked with the standard axioms only. These checks do not certify the analytic proofs.

subproblem.title: Existence of a measurable, locally bounded tangential differential L (parent Steps 1–2)
subproblem.statement: Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, and f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on U. There is L : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q) such that (a) for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, for every subspace T_x that is a weighted approximate tangent space of (M, θ) at x and every v ∈ T_x, t ↦ f(x + tv) is differentiable at t = 0 with derivative L(x)v; (b) L is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for every compact K ⊆ U, sup_{x ∈ M ∩ K} ‖L(x)‖ < ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P Q n : ℕ) (U M : Set (Eucl P)) (θ : Eucl P → ℝ) (ξ : Eucl P → NVector (Eucl P) n) (f : Eucl P → Eucl Q), IsOpen U → IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → ∃ L : Eucl P → (Eucl P →L[ℝ] Eucl Q), (∀ᵐ x ∂((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M), ∀ Tx : Submodule ℝ (Eucl P), HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x Tx → ∀ v ∈ Tx, HasDerivAt (fun t : ℝ => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable L ((μHE[n] : Measure (Eucl P)).restrict M) ∧ ∀ K : Set (Eucl P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ x ∈ M ∩ K, ‖L x‖ ≤ C
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions used below. ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with inner product ⟨·,·⟩ and norm |·|; Hⁿ = μHE[n] (Mathlib's Euclidean-normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure; on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume, it is invariant under isometries and translations and scales by λⁿ under x ↦ λx). An n-covector α is a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ with the operator norm ‖α‖ (least C with |α(u₁,…,u_n)| ≤ C Π|u_i|); an n-vector is a continuous linear functional on n-covectors with the operator norm; simpleNVector v is the n-vector α ↦ α(v₁,…,v_n), so |simpleNVector v (α)| ≤ ‖α‖ Π|v_i|; for a linear map A, A_# w := nVectorPushforward n A w = w ∘ A^#, where A^#α = α(A·,…,A·), it is linear in w and A_#(simpleNVector v) = simpleNVector(A v) (`nVectorPushforward_simple`). A map Φ is c-antilipschitz on Ω if c|w − w′| ≤ |Φ(w) − Φ(w′)| for all w, w′ ∈ Ω.

This is Steps 1–2 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 3 §2, 2.1–2.2 and p. 76), with the C¹ decomposition supplied by the siblings. Setting: U ⊆ ℝ^P open, IsRectifiableTriple U n M θ ξ, f locally Lipschitz on U. We use the elementary fact
(DD) (Directional derivatives along a chart; Simon Ch. 2, 4.7–4.10, and Step 2 of the parent proof.) Let f be K-Lipschitz on a ball B_ρ(x) ⊆ ℝ^P, let Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P be differentiable at w with Φ(w) = x, and let f∘Φ be differentiable at w. Then for every s ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) is differentiable at t = 0 with derivative D(f∘Φ)(w)s, and |D(f∘Φ)(w)s| ≤ K|DΦ(w)s|. Proof: as t → 0, both x + t·DΦ(w)s and Φ(w + ts) tend to x, so they lie in B_ρ(x) for small |t|; then |f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(Φ(w+ts))| ≤ K|Φ(w) + t·DΦ(w)s − Φ(w+ts)| = o(t) by differentiability of Φ at w, and f(Φ(w+ts)) = f(x) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t) by differentiability of f∘Φ at w. Hence f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) = f(x) + t·D(f∘Φ)(w)s + o(t). Finally |f(x + t·DΦ(w)s) − f(x)| ≤ K|t||DΦ(w)s| for small t, so the derivative has norm ≤ K|DΦ(w)s|.

1. (Charts.) By the sibling lemma countably_rectifiable_c1_cover applied to the countably n-rectifiable set M (field `countablyRectifiable`) there are C¹ maps Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P and open Ω_j ⊆ ℝⁿ such that Φ_j is K_j-Lipschitz and c_j-antilipschitz on Ω_j and Hⁿ(M ∖ ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)) = 0. Replace Ω_j by the open set Ω_j ∩ Φ_j⁻¹(U); all properties persist and, as M ⊆ U, the covering property is unchanged. Each Φ_j(Ω_j) is σ-compact, hence Borel, and Ψ_j := (Φ_j|Ω_j)⁻¹ : Φ_j(Ω_j) → Ω_j is (1/c_j)-Lipschitz, in particular continuous. Put P_j := Φ_j(Ω_j) ∖ ⋃_{i<j} Φ_i(Ω_i) (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_j P_j = ⋃_j Φ_j(Ω_j)), and u_j := f∘Φ_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^Q.

2. (Definition of L.) For x ∈ P_j let w := Ψ_j(x), A := DΦ_j(w) (injective, since |As| ≥ c_j|s| by the antilipschitz property on the open set Ω_j) and A⁺ := (A*A)⁻¹A* : ℝ^P → ℝⁿ (so A⁺A = id_{ℝⁿ}, AA⁺ = π_x, the orthogonal projection onto range A, and A⁺ = A⁺π_x); define L(x) := fderiv ℝ u_j w ∘ A⁺ (Mathlib's fderiv, which is 0 where u_j is not differentiable). For x ∉ ⋃_j P_j define L(x) := 0.

3. (Measurability.) On P_j, x ↦ L(x) is the composition of the continuous map Ψ_j, the Borel map w ↦ fderiv ℝ u_j w (Mathlib `measurable_fderiv`), the continuous map w ↦ DΦ_j(w), and the continuous map A ↦ A⁺ on the open set of injective linear maps; composition of linear maps is continuous. Hence L is Borel measurable on ℝ^P (countably many Borel pieces, 0 elsewhere), and since its values lie in the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^Q), L is strongly measurable, in particular AEStronglyMeasurable for Hⁿ⌞M.

4. (Good set.) The following sets are Hⁿ-null: (a) M ∖ ⋃_j P_j (step 1); (b) for each j, Φ_j(Z_j), where Z_j ⊆ Ω_j is the set where u_j is not differentiable: u_j is locally Lipschitz on the open set Ω_j (f locally Lipschitz on U ⊇ Φ_j(Ω_j), Φ_j Lipschitz), so by Rademacher's theorem (applied to Lipschitz extensions of u_j on countably many balls covering Ω_j; SimonGMT `rademacher_ae_differentiableAt`) Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0, and Hⁿ(Φ_j(Z_j)) ≤ K_jⁿ Lⁿ(Z_j) = 0; (c) for each j, the set of x ∈ M ∩ Φ_j(Ω_j) at which HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (range DΦ_j(Ψ_j x)) fails: by the sibling lemma weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart, applied with (Q, V, M, θ, Φ, Ω) := (P, U, M, θ, Φ_j, Ω_j), whose hypotheses are the fields `subset`, `nullMeasurableSet`, `pos`, `integrableOn` of the triple. Let G be M minus the union of these null sets; Hⁿ(M ∖ G) = 0.

5. (The derivative clause.) Let x ∈ G, so x ∈ P_j for some j; put w := Ψ_j(x), A := DΦ_j(w), B := Du_j(w) (u_j is differentiable at w as x ∉ Φ_j(Z_j)). Let T_x be any subspace with HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x T_x. Since also HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x (range A) (x ∉ set (c)) and θ(x) > 0 (x ∈ M), uniqueness (`HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique`) gives T_x = range A. For v ∈ T_x write v = As with s := A⁺v. Since U is open and f is locally Lipschitz on U, f is K-Lipschitz on some ball B_ρ(x) ⊆ U; by (DD), t ↦ f(x + tv) has derivative Bs at t = 0, and L(x)v = B A⁺ A s = Bs. Thus HasDerivAt (fun t => f (x + t • v)) (L x v) 0 for all v ∈ T_x. As Hⁿ(M ∖ G) = 0, this holds for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x.

6. (Local bound.) Let K ⊆ U be compact. For each z ∈ K choose ρ_z > 0 and K_z with B_{2ρ_z}(z) ⊆ U and f K_z-Lipschitz on B_{2ρ_z}(z) (U open, f locally Lipschitz on U). Finitely many balls B_{ρ_{z_l}}(z_l) cover K; let C := max_l K_{z_l} and ρ := min_l ρ_{z_l}. For x ∈ K, B_ρ(x) ⊆ B_{2ρ_l}(z_l) for an l with x ∈ B_{ρ_l}(z_l), so f is C-Lipschitz on B_ρ(x). Now let x ∈ M ∩ K. If x ∉ ⋃_j P_j, L(x) = 0. If x ∈ P_j, with w, A, A⁺ as in step 2: if u_j is not differentiable at w then L(x) = 0; otherwise, for v ∈ ℝ^P put s := A⁺v, so As = π_x v, and by (DD) |L(x)v| = |Du_j(w)s| ≤ C|As| = C|π_x v| ≤ C|v|. Hence ‖L(x)‖ ≤ C for all x ∈ M ∩ K.

Steps 3, 5 and 6 are the three conjuncts of the conclusion. ∎ (For n = 0 the same construction gives L ≡ 0 on the good set, since A⁺ = 0 and range A = {0}; for n > P, Hⁿ ≡ 0 on ℝ^P and the clauses are trivial; the proof above covers both cases.)
proof_key_steps: Take the C¹ antilipschitz Lipschitz charts (Φ_j, Ω_j) of M from countably_rectifiable_c1_cover, restricted to Φ_j⁻¹(U), and disjoint Borel pieces P_j.
Define L(x) := D(f∘Φ_j)(Ψ_j x) ∘ DΦ_j(Ψ_j x)⁺ on P_j (Moore–Penrose left inverse), 0 elsewhere; it is Borel.
Good set: Rademacher for f∘Φ_j, Lipschitz images of null sets, and the tangent identification T_x = range DΦ_j(w) from weighted_tangent_on_c1_chart plus uniqueness.
Directional-derivative computation (DD): t ↦ f(x + tAs) has derivative D(f∘Φ_j)(w)s = L(x)As, giving the HasDerivAt clause for every weighted tangent space at x.
Local bound: (DD) with a uniform Lipschitz constant on a finite ball cover of K gives ‖L(x)‖ ≤ C on M ∩ K.

audit.reason: The chartwise pseudoinverse construction gives measurable L. Rademacher, tangent identification, and uniqueness establish the derivative clause for every admissible tangent space. The directional estimate also bounds L at every point of M ∩ K, including points outside the almost-everywhere good set, as required by the stronger final conjunct.
